summary.oneLiner: Khazanchi delivered a landmark FY26 — total income up 15.7% to INR2,051 cr but profit nearly doubling (PAT +98.9% to INR89.4 cr, EBITDA margin +253bps to 6.19%) as the company deliberately mix-shifted from low-margin B2B wholesale toward higher-margin designer jewellery, diamonds (Vajraa) and a newly opened large-format Chennai retail showroom. The structural bet is to lift retail from ~10% to ~25% of sales over two years (retail margins ~10-12% vs blended ~6%), sustaining a stated 25-30% growth trajectory; near-term watch-item is the Modi-government appeal to curb gold buying + duty hikes, which management frames as a short (1-2 month) blip given gold's cultural embeddedness and household-gold recycling.

one-line thesis: Khazanchi delivered a landmark FY26 — total income up 15.7% to INR2,051 cr but profit nearly doubling (PAT +98.9% to INR89.4 cr, EBITDA margin +253bps to 6.19%) as the company deliberately mix-shifted from low-margin B2B wholesale toward higher-margin designer jewellery, diamonds (Vajraa) and a newly opened large-format Chennai retail showroom. The structural bet is to lift retail from ~10% to ~25% of sales over two years (retail margins ~10-12% vs blended ~6%), sustaining a stated 25-30% growth trajectory; near-term watch-item is the Modi-government appeal to curb gold buying + duty hikes, which management frames as a short (1-2 month) blip given gold's cultural embeddedness and household-gold recycling.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | H2/FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total income (FY26) | INR2,051.02 cr | +15.71% | Full-year |
| Total income (H2 FY26) | INR1,098.26 cr | +8.1% | Half-year |
| EBITDA (FY26) | INR126.99 cr | +95.69% | Margin 6.19% (+253bps YoY) |
| EBITDA (H2 FY26) | INR73.21 cr | +102.79% | Margin 6.67% (+312bps YoY) |
| PAT (FY26) | INR89.42 cr | +98.87% | Margin 4.36% (+182bps YoY) |
| PAT (H2 FY26) | INR50.72 cr | +103.6% | Margin 4.62% (+217bps YoY) |
| EPS (FY26) | INR36.10 | +98.57% | H2 EPS INR20.46 (+103.18%) |
| Inventory | ~INR400-408 cr | up | Rose on stocking the new retail store (~2 months old) |
| Working capital cycle | 52 days | — | Inventory ~70-75 days; receivables collected within ~1 week |
> No one-off accounting distortions flagged. Profit growth is genuine operating leverage + mix-shift (low-margin → high-margin/designer/diamond). Margins are thin in absolute terms (jewellery norm); profit nearly doubled off a low base.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** 25-30% "at the constraint level" (management says it has historically beaten this); for FY27 reiterated 25-30%, with one comment that PAT confidence is "35%".
- **Margin:** Blended margins to keep improving via mix-shift; retail margin bracket ~10-12%; expects bottom-line improvement to outpace top line.
- **Retail mix:** lift retail from ~10% to ~25% of total sales within ~2 financial years.
- **New flagship store:** target revenue INR450-500 cr from the Chennai showroom in the near future; retail inventory turns expected 3-4x.
- **Expansion:** smaller-format stores first in/around Tamil Nadu, then pan-India; funded internally (no fundraising planned currently).
- **Inventory:** mentioned inventory could rise toward ~INR440-450 cr (~10% jump) as retail scales.
order book & pipeline:
- Not an order-book business. Demand visibility framed via: >1,000 (active ~500) repeat B2B clients (~80% repeat; ~40-50 churn / +~100 added per year; no single client >5% of volume); retail footfall at the new Chennai flagship described as strong/repeating.
- Avg retail invoice (ticket) size ~INR1.5-1.7 lakh; wholesale ticket undefined (varies client-to-client).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **B2B wholesale (legacy core, ~90% of sales currently):** diversified jeweller clientele across India (small jewellers to pan-India chain stores), strong in South India; differentiation = in-house design library + asset-light manufacturing network. Handmade jewellery adds value/margin.
- **B2C retail (growth engine):** flagship 10,000 sq ft Chennai showroom (~6,800 sq ft selling area), opened ~2 months before the call (~Apr 2026); too early for sales/sq-ft metric. Target INR450-500 cr.
- **Vajraa Diamonds (premiumization brand):** diamond jewellery push gaining traction with customers and trade; key bottom-line contributor.
- **Manufacturing:** asset-light — designs created in-house, production outsourced to artisan factories spread across India; finishing/fusion done in-house. Gold bullion procured from direct sources.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Premiumization via diamond (Vajraa) and premium silver in B2C.
- Omni-channel: B2B + B2C + e-commerce (planned) to build a balanced revenue mix.
- Pan-India retail rollout beyond Tamil Nadu (smaller-format stores).
- ERP-driven demand analytics to optimize design/stock mix.
- Lightweight & low-carat designs as a hedge against high gold prices.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Margin expansion driven by mix-shift to higher-margin designer/diamond items and retail (10-12% vs blended ~6%).
- B2B margins flexed product-to-product: new products carry higher margin; competitive SKUs are price-trimmed to retain clients — net "blend" keeps margins improving (denies sacrificing B2B margin to acquire customers).
- Gold-price moves: claims inventory-management + buy-back/pricing policy insulate margins even on a 15-20% gold-price fall; rising gold favours lightweight/low-carat SKUs.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- New flagship store already operational. Future expansion = smaller stores in TN then pan-India, on internal accruals (no debt/equity raise planned now).
- No large manufacturing capex (asset-light); main "capex" is store rollout + retail inventory build.
capital allocation:
- Internal funding for expansion; no fundraising planned. Inventory build for retail is the main capital use.
- No dividend / buyback commentary on the call.
risks & watch-items:
- **Policy/sentiment:** PM Modi's appeal to halt gold buying for a year + import-duty hikes (CAD/currency management) — mgmt expects only a 1-2 month top-line blip, no margin impact; gold-monetization/recycling could offset via exchange business. VERIFY actual H1 FY27 demand.
- **High gold prices** may dampen discretionary volume; mitigated by lightweight/low-carat designs and exchange.
- **Retail execution risk:** unproven large-format retail economics (store only ~2 months old; INR450-500 cr target aggressive); South India is highly competitive.
- **Inventory build** lengthening days/working capital as retail scales.
- **Customer concentration low** (no client >5%) — a positive, but B2B is price-competitive.
- **Single management voice** (only the Chairman/JMD spoke; answers often qualitative/repetitive, light on hard numbers).
management quality / tone: - Confident, promotional, repetitive ("constraint level… 25-30%" repeated many times); leans on "5-decade legacy" and design capability. Light on quantitative specifics (declined sales/sq-ft, vague on volume-vs-price split, slipped between "70-75 days inventory" and "52 days working capital"). One stray "PAT… 35%" remark not clearly substantiated. CFO present but silent. Tone optimistic on retail and dismissive of policy risk — treat guidance with caution and verify next quarter.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The near-doubling of PAT on only ~16% revenue growth is the story: pure operating leverage + mix-shift, not volume. Sustainability hinges on retail actually reaching 25% of sales at 10-12% margins.
- Asset-light model = high return ratios / low capex, but also limited moat vs other organized jewellers; the claimed moat is the in-house design library + artisan sourcing network.
- Margins remain structurally thin (~6% EBITDA) — this is a high-volume, low-margin jeweller premiumizing, not a luxury-margin brand.
- Policy overhang (Modi gold-buying appeal + duties) is the key swing factor for H1 FY27 demand; management's "no impact" stance is the thing to falsify next quarter.

themes.title: Jewellery & wedding-economy formalization
themes.need: Organized jewellery is gaining share via capital-light FOCO expansion and GST/hallmarking formalization, even amid record gold-price volatility. KALYANKJIL posted Q4 revenue +66% YoY with 150 new FY27 stores and a near-zero non-GML-debt target; SENCO/PNGJL/DPABHUSHAN ride regional formalization; SKYGOLD/RGL/GOLDIAM on B2B and lab-grown export; KALAMANDIR on the wedding-wear economy.
themes.driver: Akshaya Tritiya / wedding-season demand; FOCO store rollout; gold-price stabilization lifting volumes.
